main_body: A grey stove: a light grey top slab (rows 9-12) with two dark studs, above a tall slate front panel (rows 14-29) holding a dark firebox opening with a flame inside.
top_band: light grey-blue #a0acb8 rows 9-11, with a lighter edge row 12 (#d0d8e0). It is only 3-4 rows and reads as a flat plate or a lighter panel header, not a surface seen from above.
evidence: Column x=8 reads: outline row 8, light band rows 9-11, edge highlight row 12, dark line row 13, then the slate front rows 14-29. The firebox is a dark rectangle with a flame, drawn face-on. The top band is a narrow header strip with two studs, the same width as the body, and it is not a foreshortened horizontal surface. The firebox is drawn flat with no visible interior depth. The whole piece is a front elevation with a light band on top, so it fails.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 10 distinct colours and a median of 7 colours per tile, against 38-40 distinct colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. About 60% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline leans near-black. The slate front panel (4 rows of one tone, 16 rows tall) and the dark firebox are large single-tone areas with no grain or speckle. The flame has some steps, but the rest is shallow and sticker-like next to the references.
